c0_prohib.instructions: Read this part of the order: «Feuerstein, the artillery will bombard the Prussian columns on the Kaiserstrasse.». Is it a prohibition or a limit, telling someone what not to do or how far not to go ('do not charge the line without my order', 'not to be drawn beyond X', 'attack nothing', 'only on my express order'), rather than an instruction to do something?

criteria.true: yes, it forbids or limits something
criteria.false: no, it is an instruction to act, or information

c0_forbid.instructions: Read this part of the order: «Feuerstein, the artillery will bombard the Prussian columns on the Kaiserstrasse.». If it forbids or limits something, what is forbidden?

criteria.none: nothing in particular is forbidden, or it is not a prohibition
criteria.charge_formed_infantry: not to charge the enemy's formed infantry: his line, his battalions, his squares, the troops on the heights
criteria.attack: not to attack or assault at all, or only on a further order ('attack nothing', 'come into the attack only on my order')
criteria.pursue: not to pursue or follow up a beaten or fleeing enemy
criteria.advance_beyond: not to go beyond or farther than a certain place, not to be drawn off
criteria.engage: not to engage, fight, halt or turn against the enemy, or be drawn into a fight

c0_trig.instructions: Read this part of the order: «Feuerstein, the artillery will bombard the Prussian columns on the Kaiserstrasse.». Does it tie what it orders to an event or a time?

criteria.none: no event or time is named: it is to be done at once, or it is a standing rule
criteria.start: it is to be done only when or after something happens or a time comes ('as soon as', 'once', 'when', 'after', 'at <time>')
criteria.until: it is to last only until something happens or a time comes ('until', 'till')

c0_event.instructions: Read this part of the order: «Feuerstein, the artillery will bombard the Prussian columns on the Kaiserstrasse.». If it names an event or a time on which what it orders starts or ends, what is that event?

criteria.reached: a formation reaches, takes, holds or passes a place
criteria.engaged: a formation is engaged with the enemy or attacks
criteria.seen: the enemy comes into sight or approaches
criteria.routs: some body breaks, flees or gives way
criteria.order: a further order from the commander arrives

c0_who.instructions: Read this part of the order: «Feuerstein, the artillery will bombard the Prussian columns on the Kaiserstrasse.». If it names such an event, whom does the event concern: which formation must reach or hold the place, be engaged, or break?
